issues.issue: The first GEMSDOE25 'recommended' submission (gems25-factorial-best-v1-nan.tif, sha256 fbef100f...) used an invented footprint: 2,344,929 of the 5,167,373 pixels in the pinned owner-mirror template footprint are NaN and 2,832,257 pixels outside it are finite. NaN fails every 0<=x<=1 test, consistent with the user-reported portal message 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]'.
issues.evidence: evidence/old_gems25_tif_forensics.json (recomputed from git history, commit 9b01f27, against the pinned owner-mirror template; not organizer-authenticated)
issues.resolution_or_action: File removed. src/gems25/submission.py takes the footprint from the template mirror, refuses NaN inside it, and check_file() reproduces the local failure (tests/test_submission.py). Cause is an inference from mirrored data, not confirmed by DrivenData; neither the template nor portal validator is organizer-authenticated here.

issues.issue: The same file emitted 1,249,834 positive pixels (624,029 inside the footprint = 12.1 % of it; 625,805 outside it), roughly 10x the 2.34 % budget of H19-5 and 21x the dotted file's 60,069 pixels. At the measured truth density the false-positive term would swamp the score. The old site nevertheless said 'FORMAT VERIFIED' and the README credited the dot-thinning of the 0.2477 file.
issues.resolution_or_action: Replaced by files whose emission is justified by the metric algebra and the hide-and-recover results.

issues.issue: Previous scripts were non-functional or misleading: generate_submission.py wrote synthetic diagonal stripes inside an elliptical made-up footprint; ridge_detector.py was a toy; factorial_design.py never ran (no data); the README listed src/feature_families.py, src/emission_policies.py and reference_solution/ that did not exist; the page's 'Footprint all finite / All checks pass' described a file that failed them.
issues.resolution_or_action: Removed from the working tree (kept in history). Replaced by tested modules under src/gems25 and executed experiments.

issues.issue: The old scripts/dti_metric.py used kernel 1 - d/(R+0.5) with R = 3 px (support 3.5 px). The official kernel is max(1 - d/R, 0) with R = 300 m = 3 px.
issues.resolution_or_action: src/gems25/metric.py implements the published equations; tests compare it with a brute-force transcription.

issues.issue: Band 6 'tc' of the mirrored training_features.tif is described as 'Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection', but its values (3.7-70.6, positive) equal the official GeoDAWN radiometric total count channel: Spearman 0.9999 against the USGS-release TC grid (and 0.89/0.91/0.72 with K/Th/U).
issues.resolution_or_action: Band treated as radiometric TC and placed in family D (geochemical). The embedded description is wrong; do not rely on other descriptions without checking.

issues.issue: Other band descriptions disagree with the organizers' page: 'deq_n100a15' = 'Distance to earthquake' vs official 'Density of earthquakes' (and two earthquake bands vs one official layer); 'depth_to_base_surf' = 'Depth to basement surface' vs official 'depth to conductive base surface'; no band is named as the 'top-of-crustal magnetic source depth estimate' (mag_anom is an nT anomaly).
issues.resolution_or_action: Family assignment (A potential-field, C strain/seismicity, D conductivity) is a design choice and documented in src/gems25/families.py. Semantics unverified.

issues.issue: The feature raster's valid mask differs from the template footprint: 3,061 in-footprint pixels are nodata and 1,540 pixels outside the footprint are finite (the same anomaly seen in early 5GEMSDOE files).
issues.resolution_or_action: Features are NaN-aware; every submission uses the template footprint and is finite in [0,1] at all 5,167,373 footprint pixels.

issues.issue: The mirrored sample_submission.tif has 60,988 pixels equal to 1 exactly on the labelled fault pixels; the page says the sample 'predicts total fault absence'.

issues.issue: The frozen hide-and-recover comparator 0.15200338908786984 (evidence/addons/emk_extension.json, variant sapd2.4 at kfrac 0.035, base BDE + the seven add-ons, draws 0-1) does NOT reproduce in this environment. Re-running that exact arm here gives 0.149667509 (fold 0 identical to 9 decimals; folds 1-3 differ by +0.0023, -0.0042, -0.0074). Re-running a single cell in isolation reproduces this session's value bit-for-bit, so this session's pipeline is deterministic; the drift is environmental. data/work is a gitignored derived cache (static_ABCD.npy, addons.npy, bands/) that this session rebuilt with numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1, rasterio 1.4.4, and no hash of it was ever recorded, so the previous cache cannot be compared.

issues.resolution_or_action: Policy change recorded in knowledge/10 section 12.5: absolute comparators do not transfer between environments, so a promotion gate must recompute its comparator in the same run as the candidate. evidence/work_cache_hashes.json now exists so the next session can detect a rebuilt cache immediately. The frozen 0.152003389 is retained as the historical record and no arm was promoted on the strength of this drift.

issues.issue: The GEMSDOE9 raster whose file name says PLACEHOLDER (sha256 2314b599..., owner-reported 0.0107) holds 196,132 pixels of value 1.0 OUTSIDE the owner-mirror template footprint, plus 6,915,655 zeros; it has no NaN. issues.issue: A single-band truth-intensity model based only on distance to known faults does not fit 25 hash-linked owner-reported DTI anchors: leave-one-artifact-out RMSE 0.0705–0.0812 (pre-registered threshold 0.020), blind-lattice prediction 0.2057 vs owner-reported 0.0904, and worst residual −0.1787. The score claims remain unverified; residuals indicate model misspecification relative to these claims and cannot be attributed solely to detector skill.
issues.resolution_or_action: Closed as a conditional negative result: the tested distance-to-known-faults habitat model did not satisfy its adoption rule, and no submission was designed from it. The fitted model does not support "hug the known-fault halo" as a promotion strategy. The anchor-based calibration remains conditional on unverified owner-reported scores and does not identify actual hidden-label locations.

issues.issue: The single-band model fitted conditionally on 25 hash-linked owner-reported scores matches several in-band claims and the blind lattice within 0.004 DTI, but under-predicts owner-mirrored off-band surfaces: h25-ctx-ridge 0.0907 predicted vs 0.1280 reported, h28-dotted-ridge 0.1251 vs 0.1839, and lidarscarp-top2pct has model-implied N 22,893 vs 12,691 for the H19-5 family. These residuals show model-scope/misspecification risk relative to unverified claims; they do not establish where actual hidden labels lie or validate off-band scores. The two-band mixture was not identified (nine-anchor spread 0.514 vs 0.053; mean absolute residual worse, 0.0335 vs 0.0172).
issues.resolution_or_action: Print this scope limit wherever predictions appear (README, site, knowledge/10). Treat off-band surfaces only as conditional-model exploration priorities, not evidence that hidden truth exists there. The current H30 register is separate and requires its own paired catalogue-gap proxy test.

issues.issue: The official reference solution keeps a patch only where 'valid elevation data (channel 4)' is finite, i.e. channel INDEX 4 = the 5th band. In the owner mirror the 5th band's own TIFF tag reads 'Isostatic gravity anomaly slope' (category gravity_data) and detrended elevation is band 12. Read literally that would mean the mirror's band order does not match the organizer's file, which would shift every feature-family assignment in this repository.
issues.evidence: COMPUTED this session: per-band non-finite masks of all 19 cached bands are IDENTICAL for 18 of 19 bands (7,112,688 non-finite pixels each, i.e. exactly the area outside the 5,167,373-px footprint); the single exception is band 6 ('tc'), which differs from band 5 by 12 pixels of 12,279,292. Source: github.com/drivendataorg/gems-prize-reference-solution, notebook cell 12.
issues.resolution_or_action: Closed: channel 4 in the reference is a data-validity proxy, not an elevation claim - because the non-finite mask is the same for every band, testing channel 4 is equivalent to testing any channel. No band-order discrepancy exists; the mirror's own per-band tags (which the reference solution itself reads) remain the band semantics of record (evidence/band_semantics.json, knowledge/08).

issues.issue: The official reference solution writes its submission as a single-band float32 GeoTIFF using the labels' CRS and transform and sets NO nodata tag, so its file is finite everywhere (zeros outside the study area). This repository's primary download instead writes NaN outside the footprint to match the owner-mirrored sample_submission.tif, and ships a zeros-outside fallback. The two conventions differ and the portal's validator is not public.
issues.evidence: github.com/drivendataorg/gems-prize-reference-solution notebook cell 19 (rasterio.open(..., 'w', dtype=y_final.dtype, crs=..., transform=...); no nodata= argument); the owner-mirrored template has NaN outside the footprint; the GEMSDOE9 PLACEHOLDER mirror holds 196,132 pixels of value 1.0 outside the footprint and is nonetheless reported scored (IR-25-PLACEHOLDER-OUTSIDE-FOOTPRINT).
issues.resolution_or_action: Both files are already published on the download page: the NaN-outside primary (matching the template) and the zeros-outside fallback (matching the official reference's convention). If the portal ever rejects one, submit the other; neither has been organizer-verified. No change to the shipped bytes was made on this evidence.

issues.issue: The official reference solution submits continuous averaged probabilities and its author notes 'it may be advantageous to threshold this map for better scoring'. This repository proves a stronger statement and had already been shipping binary emissions.
issues.evidence: notebook cells 17 and 20 (y_final continuous; the third panel plots y_final > 0.1); the binary-optimality lemma recorded in evidence/h28_calibration/design.json ('binary_optimality_lemma'): for a fixed support the DTI is a linear-fractional function of p, so the optimum is bang-bang and soft values in (0,1) cannot beat a binary emission.
issues.resolution_or_action: Closed as corroboration: the organizer's own benchmark points the same way as the algebra. Every file this repo ships is binary 0/1, and the lemma is now stated wherever the emission design is described.
